events.title: Rodolfo Robles selective physical gate blockade during migrant caravan, October2018
events.endpoint_type: unknown
events.scope: Rodolfo Robles bridge entry into Mexico for caravan participants; no bilateral frontier-wide prohibition.
events.crossings: Rodolfo Robles bridge; Tecún Umán–Ciudad Hidalgo
events.movement: Caravan participants seeking entry without migration documents; selected applicants admitted. Later vehicle restriction separately described but its onset/end unknown.
events.exceptions: Morning asylum applicants admitted; children and adults admitted in groups after afternoon closure. River crossings occurred. No all-person prohibition asserted.
events.imposing_authority: Mexican Federal Police and immigration authorities
events.enforcement: Police physically shut metal gate and prevented mass passage; beyond routine document checks alone.
events.consequences: People remained on bridge or crossed river; no quantified harm or displacement estimate assigned.
events.relationship: Part-promotion of R3-AM-L007 October2018 component; January20 2020 component remains unresolved and distinct from R3-AM-007. October28 candidate held for overlap.
events.status_observation: Historical episode; no current-status inference.
events.official_rationale: Authorities sought ordered admission under migration/refugee procedures rather than mass undocumented passage.
events.context: Caravan confrontation and physical gate barricade; Guatemalan preceding barrier reported but not separately counted.
events.uncertainty: Official morning denial is preserved alongside later physical blockade; these concern different times and blanket versus selective scope. Same-day admissions prevent continuous total-closure inference. November7 pedestrian reopening report is only normal-by evidence; vehicles remained barred then. October28 possible renewed phase is held separately.

events.scope: Inbound commercial cargo entering the Beitbridge border area from South Africa toward Zimbabwe

events.imposing_authority: Protesting transporters and travelers; non-state physical blockade
events.enforcement: Report says travelers, many in private cars, deliberately blocked commercial cargo vehicles; security personnel intervened.
events.consequences: Vehicle queues and congestion reported; causal share attributable to blockade not quantified.
events.relationship: Incidental off-assignment discovery for South Africa/Zimbabwe 2018; not credited as completed search of that cell. Separate unresolved earlier June scanner-yard protest is R15-AS-L004.

events.title: Pino Hachado and Icalma reported closure during Chilean customs strike, May 2017
events.endpoint_type: unknown
events.scope: Named international land crossings Pino Hachado and Icalma; not the whole Argentina–Chile frontier
events.direction: Motorists on Argentine approach at Pino Hachado were reportedly told to return. Bilateral scope and Icalma direction unresolved.
events.movement: Pino Hachado motorists reported turned back; Icalma described unavailable. Full nationality, passenger/freight and directional categories not established.
events.exceptions: ANFACH stated exceptional emergency shifts continued nationally. Customs reported priority cargo contingency; local exemptions at these two posts not established.
events.imposing_authority: Striking Chilean customs personnel (ANFACH); Argentine Gendarmería reported redirecting motorists
events.enforcement: LM Neuquén quotes Escuadrón Las Lajas on actual turnbacks; Río Negro quotes Vialidad Nacional that both passes were unavailable for non-road-condition reasons. No direct researcher observation.
events.relationship: No matching May 2017 customs-strike event or Pino Hachado/Icalma lead found in current629-event/271-lead register.
events.status_observation: Contemporaneous May 2017 evidence only; no present-status inference.
events.official_rationale: ANFACH attributed strike to disputed staffing and career-reclassification commitments. Chilean Customs sought to maintain traffic through contingency staffing.
events.context: Intentional strike-related interruption of border processing; concrete motorist turnbacks attributed to Gendarmería at Pino Hachado. Same/next-day opening reports are preserved.
events.uncertainty: DiarioAndino May 24 headline lists Pino Hachado open; Río Negro May 25 reports open posts and says strike did not cause regional closures, while DiarioAndino May 25 still calls Pino Hachado/Icalma strike total. events.title: Inherited Finland–Norway restriction on ordinary cross-border reindeer husbandry
events.endpoint_type: unresolved
events.scope: Finland–Norway land-frontier husbandry/grazing regime; treaty fence line is the operative divide where specified, with the international boundary operative between Angeli and boundary cairn 343.
events.crossings: Frontier grazing areas; not general passenger checkpoints
events.movement: Reindeer crossing the treaty-defined divide for ordinary husbandry/grazing, subject to designated-route and lawful slaughter-import exceptions.
events.exceptions: Articles 7–11 regulate recovery/return of strays. Article 19 permits commission-designated migration routes across the other state, without grazing during that movement, and excludes lawfully imported slaughter reindeer under secure guarding. Fence deviations mean the operative grazing divide is not everywhere the international line. No general passenger or all-livestock trade ban asserted.
events.imposing_authority: Norwegian and Finnish authorities under bilateral reindeer conventions
events.enforcement: Bilateral fences, owner guarding duties and regulated return of straying reindeer; legal policy and physical compliance are distinguished.
events.relationship: Promoted from R15-EU-L002. 2017 treaty renewal is not a newly dated closure.
events.status_observation: Agricultural authority page updated 13 September 2024 describes the exclusion; no 2026 cutoff extension inferred.
events.official_rationale: The Norwegian government’s treaty explanation states that the convention allocates responsibilities for fences and other measures to prevent reindeer crossing the Finland–Norway boundary and for handling incursions. This is a known husbandry and boundary-administration reason outside the current rationale taxonomy.
events.context: Historical seasonal grazing movement; fence coverage and legal prohibition have different timelines.
events.uncertainty: Historical effective onset unknown; 1852 declaration did not immediately end grazing, and January 1 2017 renews the treaty. The narrow legal husbandry regime is evidenced, not perfect physical enforcement, every commercial import condition, or a prohibition on the explicit treaty exceptions.

Treaty Articles 1–3 establish guarding/fence regime and fence-defined operative boundary except Angeli–boundary cairn 343. Article 19 expressly permits commission-designated migration routes without grazing, and excludes lawfully imported slaughter reindeer under secure guarding. These exceptions must be explicit.

[REC-R16-EU-001-S003] Historical chronology access | full | Publication date unknown
Articles 1–3 define guarding/fence duties and the operative boundary; Article 19 allows commission-designated migration routes without grazing and securely guarded lawful slaughter imports. Article 26 gives a thirty-year treaty term and Article 27 replaces the 1981 convention. The prospective term is not treated as demonstrated enforcement or future closure.

[REV-R16-EU-001-S003] Historical chronology access | full | Publication date unknown
Article 19 permits commission-designated migration routes without grazing and guarded lawful slaughter imports; other clauses require guarding and stray-return arrangements.

[FU-R16-EU-001-01] Follow-up research | full | Publication date unknown
Articles 1–3 establish guarding and fence arrangements preventing reindeer incursions; Articles 11–12 regulate unlawful grazing and damage compensation; Article 19 preserves designated migration routes and lawful slaughter imports. No disease rationale established.

[FC4-R16-EU-001-01] Follow-up challenge | full | Publication date unknown
Article 1 obliges owners to guard herds against crossing and explains fences as supporting that duty. This is a husbandry arrangement; no disease or market-protection justification appears in the inspected purpose clauses.

The restriction is on travel out of Sudan through Gallabat towards Ethiopia. Goods remain allowed; returned victims and other-country crossings are not additional closure cohorts. Retain the 19–20 November onset bound and last-confirmed 20 November. No matched reopening was found in the bounded retrieval; a last-confirmed day is not an endpoint or proof of continuous restriction to the study end. Reported passenger safety and robbery concerns support the existing Security assignments. The evidence does not support a goods prohibition or a new trade rationale. Dabanga and Sagia passages were directly read; Sudan Tribune’s exact-URL text was indexed after a direct 404. Possible shared reporting origin remains explicit; no multiple-origin certainty is claimed. The phase remains unlocated with no invented Gallabat coordinate.
